stemMarkdown: How many trailing zeroes does $365!$ have?
solutionMarkdown: Each trailing zero needs a factor of 10, and 5s are scarcer than 2s, so count the 5s: \left\lfloor \dfrac{365}{5} \right\rfloor = 73 , \left\lfloor \dfrac{365}{25} \right\rfloor = 14 , \left\lfloor \dfrac{365}{125} \right\rfloor = 2. Adding these gives $89$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Higher powers of 5 must be counted again — 25 contributes two 5s, 125 contributes three.
